title: RE Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1: Yes; lower court reversed in whole and complaint sustained as to the Administrative Commission's calling/facilitating the 2/18/2001 congregational meeting and recognizing a session based on it. Issue 2: Yes; lower court reversed in whole and complaint sustained as to KEP's 3/2/2001 approval of those actions.
first_summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Korean Eastern Presbytery and reversed the presbytery's approval of its administrative commission's February 18, 2001 congregational meeting. It held the presbytery acted beyond BCO limits by calling the meeting when the deadlocked session had failed to act; the proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43. It did not rule on the legal effect of the meeting.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint by two ruling elders against Korean Eastern Presbytery over a disputed congregational meeting (three commissioners dissented). The session was deadlocked and had not called a requested meeting; KEP's administrative commission called and supervised the February 18, 2001 meeting, and KEP approved that action. The SJC reversed both lower-court actions, holding that BCO 25-2 places responsibility on the session and that the presbytery's proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43, not act for the session. It declined to rule on the meeting's legal effect.

sources.supports: Canonical case ID, dual issues and yes answers, reversal/sustaining, BCO 25-2/13-9 and BCO 43 reasoning, refusal to rule on congregational vote's legal effect, and dissent/absence vote totals.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2001-06, RE Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery, SJC, 31st GA (2003); adopted roll call lines 144–148, with 15 concur, 3 dissent, 1 disqualified, 4 absent. Lines 140 and 144–148 identify the panel/full SJC drafting and adoption.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 16–27, 72–76: CPC's session was deadlocked and disputes arose after TE Choon Shik Kim's deposition; KEP's administrative commission called and supervised a 2/18/2001 congregational meeting to elect elders/trustees, and KEP approved it on 3/2/2001. The complainants were ruling elders not elected and challenged those actions.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 78–82: both issues answered Yes; lower court reversed in whole and complaint sustained. Lines 104–138: BCO 25-2 places responsibility to call a congregational meeting on the Session; if it fails/refuses, the remedy is complaint under BCO 43. KEP should have adjudicated the complaint, not appointed an administrative commission to act for the Session. BCO 13-9 does not give unlimited power; precedents reaffirmed. Lines 130–132 disclaim any ruling on the legal effect of the congregation's vote.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 132–138 and 144–148: the decision expressly refuses to decide the legal effect of the 2/18/2001 meeting and notes it does not override prior Ad Interim Committee precedents. Three commissioners dissented (Leopard, Lunceford, Smith), but the supplied source contains no separate dissent opinion; four were absent and one disqualified.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 110–130: Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery and Wallace W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery (M19GA, 1991, pp. 488–527) supplied the rule that a presbytery cannot suspend a session without congregation consent and due process and that PCA court jurisdiction is constitutionally limited; the Ad Interim Committee report (M14GA, 1986, pp. 103–105) supplied that a higher court may act on or against, but not for, a lower court. Lines 134–135 cite SJC Case 2001-01 for a more detailed BCO 25-2 explanation, but that opinion is not included in this source.
